lines.text: Noodle Rush!
You are broke. You are starving. And across the street, Slurpy's Noodle Bar is serving the most delicious bowl of ramen in the whole city.
Your mission: get inside, and walk out with a steaming bowl of noodles. Are you ready to play?
Slurpy's Noodle Bar hums under a flickering neon chopstick sign.
Steam curls out of the door and dances right under your nose. Spicy miso. Your tummy does a little backflip.
Do you want to go inside?
You decide ramen can wait, and you stroll off down the block.
But the wind carries that broth smell after you, like a tiny, delicious ghost. Your stomach growls so loudly that a passing dog barks back.
Who walks away from noodles? Not a hero, that's who.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
You step inside. Warm air, clattering bowls, happy slurping. And a line of hungry people that coils around the room like a sleeping dragon.
Every time someone gets their bowl, a tiny bell dings. Ding! It's torture.
You could wait your turn like a sensible person, or try to sneak ahead. Will you wait your turn?
You duck under the rope and skip eleven people at once. The whole room goes quiet.
Hey! HEY! Nobody skips the line at Slurpy's!
The chef points his ladle at you like a wizard's staff. Two waiters march you out, and your photo goes up on the Banned From Slurpy's board.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
Patience! You can definitely fake patience for ten minutes.
You shuffle forward an inch. Then another inch. A baby three spots ahead of you learns to walk before you reach the counter.
The front of the line is so close you can smell the noodles. Do you want to keep waiting?
Just then, the little old lady in front of you wrinkles her nose.
Ah... ah... ACHOO!
Her shopping bag splits, and oranges bounce everywhere. Under the tables. Into a man's hood. One even plops into the fish tank.
Oh, my oranges! Oh dear, oh dear.
If you help her, you might lose your place in the line. Do you want to help her pick them up?
You dive into action! You crawl under the tables. You pull one out of a man's hood. And you fish one out of the actual fish tank.
The goldfish looks very offended. At last, you hand back every single orange.
What a kind young thing you are. I won't forget this, dearie.
And somehow, you didn't even lose your place. Do you want to keep waiting? I know. I keep asking.
You stare very hard at the ceiling, and pretend you didn't see a thing. Then an orange rolls right under your foot.
Whoosh! You skid across the floor like a surfer, and crash-land right at the front of the line.
Hey. Did you just skip my line?
Uh-oh. Do you want to say sorry, and go back to your place?
You stay right where you are, and give the chef your very best innocent smile.
Out! Out of my noodle bar!
Your photo goes up on the Banned From Slurpy's board, right next to a photo of a raccoon.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
Suddenly, a pigeon struts in through the door like it owns the place. It hops onto a table, snatches a boiled egg right out of a man's ramen, and takes off!
Now it's flapping straight towards you, with the egg in its beak. Do you want to try and catch the egg?
You leap into the air like a goalkeeper. The pigeon gets such a fright that it drops the egg. Got it! A perfect catch!
Ha! Nice catch, kid!
You hand the egg back to its owner. He says he's not hungry anymore. The pigeon gives you a very dirty look, and waddles back outside. Do you want to keep waiting?
You duck! The pigeon zooms over your head, and drops the egg right on top of Chef Slurpy's hat.
Who threw an egg at me?!
Everybody points at the pigeon. Chef Slurpy chases it out of the door, waving his ladle.
Do you want to keep waiting?
At last, the counter!
Hi there! What can I get you?
One spicy miso ramen, extra egg, you say, heroically.
Great choice! That's seven dollars and seventy-seven cents, please!
You dig in your pocket and find a button, some fluff, and absolutely no money. You could go and find some cash, or try to pay with something else. Do you want to go and find some money?
Quick thinking! You grab a napkin, and with a squirt of ketchup you scribble out a gift certificate. You slide it across the counter.
Nice try, Picasso. We only take real money.
Looks like you'll need to earn some. Do you want to head out and earn some real money?
You flop onto the counter and refuse to budge, hoping the cashier will crack.
Next, please!
She does not crack. Your grumbling stomach gets politely walked back out onto the sidewalk.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
Back on the sidewalk. Broke. Hungry. Seven dollars and seventy-seven cents stands between you and noodle heaven.
You could find a quick job. Or, you could play for tips on your trusty emergency kazoo. Do you want to find a job?
You whip out your kazoo and play Happy Birthday. Over. And over. And over.
A dog starts to howl. Then every dog on the block joins in. People don't give you money. They give you earmuffs.
But one lady, holding eight fluffy dogs on leads, is staring at you in amazement.
My babies are singing! Honey, you've got a gift. I'll pay you ten dollars to walk them!
Do you want to walk the dogs?
No thanks, you say. You're an artist. And you play Happy Birthday again, even louder.
The dogs howl. The pigeons flee. A man shuts his window so hard, it falls off.
By sunset, you've earned zero dollars, and nine pairs of earmuffs.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
Eight dogs. Eight leads. One of you. In ten seconds flat, the leads are tangled into one giant knot.
Somehow, you make it to the park. And then, the dogs spot a squirrel.
Every ear goes up. Every tail goes stiff. Uh-oh. Do you want to hold on tight?
You let go of the leads. Big mistake.
Eight dogs zoom off in eight different directions. One up the slide. One into the pond. One into an ice-cream van.
It takes you until midnight to find them all. And you get paid in dog slobber.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
You hold on tight! The dogs take off after the squirrel, and you fly along behind them like a water-skier with no water.
Through a picnic. Through a flower bed. And now they're heading straight for the fountain!
You could shout sit, and hope they listen. Do you want to shout sit?
You yell at the top of your lungs. SIT!
All eight dogs sit at once, and you slide along on your tummy, stopping one inch from the fountain.
Well, I never! Here's your ten dollars, honey.
Then you count the dogs. Seven, eight... nine? A scruffy little stray is gazing up at you with big, hopeful eyes.
He's not one of mine. I'll find him a home, unless you want him?
Do you want to adopt him?
Too late! The dogs drag you straight through the fountain.
When they finally flop down, panting and happy, you squelch back to their owner, dripping wet.
Look at my babies, all tuckered out! Here's your ten dollars, honey.
Then you count the dogs. Seven, eight... nine? A scruffy little stray is gazing up at you with big, hopeful eyes.
He's not one of mine. I'll find him a home, unless you want him?
Do you want to adopt him?
You scoop him up, and he licks your whole face. You name him Chopstick.
You spend your ten dollars on a collar, a squeaky toy, and the biggest bag of dog biscuits in the shop.
You never did get your noodles. But you got something even better: a best friend, who thinks you're amazing.
That's the best friend ending!
A flyer flutters down the street and slaps you right in the face.
It says: Wanted! Magician's assistant. Start today! Previous assistant vanished, and never came back.
Hmm. A job is a job. Do you want to be the magician's assistant?
You toss the flyer away. No rabbits, no top hats, no thank you.
And, as it turns out, no money either. Your stomach makes a noise like a sad trombone.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
A poster flaps on a lamp post. LOST CAT. His name is Sir Pounce. Orange. Fluffy. Extremely round. Loves fish.
In the drawing, he looks like an orange beach ball with whiskers. And at the bottom, in big letters: Reward, ten dollars!
That's noodle money! Do you want to find Sir Pounce?
Where would a round cat who loves fish go? The fish market, of course!
Fresh fish! Get your fresh fish here!
You ask the fishmonger if he's seen Sir Pounce.
Big orange fella? Round as a pumpkin? He pinched twelve sardines, and scrambled up that ladder onto the roof!
You could climb up after him, or wait down here with a sardine. Do you want to climb the ladder?
You stay on the ground, and wave a sardine in the air. Here, kitty kitty!
A cat appears. Then another. Then twenty more. Every cat in the city surrounds you. Every cat, except Sir Pounce.
They gobble up every sardine in the market, and the fishmonger chases you out with a mop.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
You climb all the way up. And there, snoozing in a sunny gutter, is the roundest cat you have ever seen. Sir Pounce!
He's far too heavy to carry down the ladder, so he'll have to follow you. You could call his name, or wiggle a sardine. Do you want to call his name?
Here, Sir Pounce, you call, in your sweetest voice. Here, kitty kitty!
Sir Pounce opens one eye. Yawns. And rolls over, knocking the ladder clean off the roof.
Cats never come when they're called. Now you're stuck up here until the fire engine arrives.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
You wiggle a sardine, and Sir Pounce follows you down the ladder, step by wobbly step, all the way to the address on the poster.
The door swings open, and out steps a very big lady in a wrestling belt.
Sir Pounce! My little baby! Oh, sweetheart, thank you!
She hands you the ten-dollar reward, then offers a swap: one of her niece's famous smoothies instead. Do you want to keep the ten dollars?
Smoothie, please! you say. It's mango and banana, with a free sticker.
It's delicious. It's gone in ten seconds. And so is your noodle money.
Your tummy growls at you. It sounds very disappointed in your choices.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
An assistant! Marvelous! I am the Magnificent Marvello!
How much does it pay, you ask.
Ten dollars, paid at the end of the show! My tremendous trick is the Vanishing Assistant, and the show starts in five minutes. Shall we rehearse first?
Marvello shows you the secret. Inside the magic box are two levers. A green one, and a red one.
When I say the magic word, pull the green lever, and you'll drop through a trapdoor. But never, ever pull the red lever.
What does the red one do, you ask?
Nobody knows.
Showtime! A crowd gathers, and you step into the box.
Abracadabra!
Quick! Do you pull the green lever?
Clunk! You drop through the trapdoor, crawl under the stage, and pop out of a barrel at the back of the crowd.
Magnificent! Here are your ten dollars, my marvelous assistant!
But the crowd won't stop cheering. Encore! Encore! Do you want to do the trick one more time?
You pull the red lever.
Nothing happens. Then the whole box starts to shake.
Boom! A hidden cannon fires you, three rabbits and a cloud of confetti high over the rooftops.
You land in the duck pond. Well. Now we know what the red lever does.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
You do the trick again. And again. And again! By sunset, the whole city is talking about the Amazing Vanishing Kid.
You're a star, my friend! A star!
When the last show ends, you race to Slurpy's. But the sign says closed. So Marvello buys you a hot dog, and honestly? It's pretty great.
That's the superstar ending!
Rehearse? Pfft. A crowd gathers, you step into the magic box, Marvello waves his wand, and you vanish. Straight into the prop cupboard, knocking over every wand on the shelf.
You're fired. Magically.
Across the street, a kid is selling smoothies from a cart, and she's making a fortune.
Smoothies! Ice-cold smoothies!
Those smoothies look VERY grabbable. But you could start a cart of your own. Do you want to start your own smoothie cart?
You grab a mango smoothie and run!
AUNTIE!
Out of a van steps her auntie, a retired wrestler known as The Blender.
Somebody touched my niece's smoothies?
She spins you around like a helicopter and plops you, very gently, into a mountain of empty cups.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
You borrow a blender and set up shop. Smoothies: seven dollars and seventy-seven cents. It's a sizzling hot day. Perfect smoothie weather!
Mine are seven dollars flat. And you get a free sticker!
Everyone goes to her cart. You need something new, something nobody else is selling. Do you want to try selling something brand new?
Bold move! You slash your price to seven dollars and seventy-six cents. One whole cent cheaper!
A tumbleweed of old receipts rolls past your empty cart. Nobody comes. Not even a pigeon.
Want to go back and try again?
You turn your cart into a pop-up art stall. Tiny problem: you have nothing to sell. But a crowd gathers anyway. You just look so confident.
A man asks you to draw a sticker for his phone. You doodle a noodle with sunglasses. It's weirdly amazing.
He pays you ten whole dollars! Ready to go and get your noodles?
Ten dollars in your hand. Honest work. Honest noodles.
You march back to Slurpy's and press your nose against the window. Inside, the broth is bubbling. It's waiting for you. Do you want to go inside?
You reach for the door. And then you hear it. An ice-cream van pulls up right behind you.
Triple chocolate swirl. Rainbow sprinkles. A wafer shaped like a unicorn. And it costs exactly ten dollars.
It's calling to you. Do you want to buy an ice cream?
You hand over all ten dollars, and the ice cream is magnificent. For about one minute.
Then it melts down your arm, a seagull steals your unicorn wafer, and you remember: you came here for noodles.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
You reach for the handle, and the door swings open, straight into your nose.
A delivery courier in a hurry. Your ten dollars flies up into the air, and flutters down into the back of a passing recycling truck.
Oh no, oh no, oh no! I'm SO sorry! Here, please, have some of my takeout!
Do you want to share his takeout?
You sit on the curb with the courier and share his takeout.
It's, um, cold fries.
They're tasty. Honestly! But part of you keeps staring at Slurpy's glowing sign, and that bowl of ramen you never got.
That's the bittersweet ending!
Thanks, but no thanks, you say, rubbing your nose. You came here for ramen, and you're getting ramen.
The recycling truck is rumbling off down the street with your money. Then you notice the kitchen's back door is propped open. Hmm.
Do you want to chase after the truck?
You sprint after the truck! It rumbles around the corner, and off down the main road.
You could keep chasing it down the road, or take a shortcut through the market. Do you want to take the shortcut?
You stick to the road, and run, and run. The truck turns left. You turn left. The truck turns right. You turn right.
Then the truck turns onto the highway, and you, very sensibly, do not.
Your ten dollars waves goodbye from the back of the truck.
Game over! Want to go back and try again?
You zoom through the market, leap over a crate of cabbages, and catch the truck at a red light. But a sharp-eyed old lady has already fished your ten dollars out of the back.
Finders keepers, dearie. But I'm not a monster. I'll just keep a little finder's fee.
She keeps two dollars and twenty-two cents, and hands you the rest. Seven dollars and seventy-eight cents. Just enough! Ready to get your bowl?
You zoom through the market, leap over a crate of cabbages, and catch the truck at a red light. A sharp-eyed old lady has already fished your ten dollars out of the back.
Wait a second. It's the orange lady from the queue!
Well, if it isn't my kind young helper! I'd normally keep a finder's fee. But not from you, dearie. Here. All ten dollars.
Being kind really does pay! Ready to go and get your bowl?
Back inside Slurpy's. And this time, there's no line at all! You march up to the counter, and slap down your money.
One spicy miso ramen, extra egg, coming up! Oh, and today only, you can make it Dragon Fire. It's so spicy, nobody has ever finished a bowl.
On the wall are photos of everybody who tried. They're all crying. Do you want to try the Dragon Fire?
The bowl arrives, glowing red. Tiny flames dance across the top.
Good luck, kid.
First slurp. Your face turns pink. Then red. Then purple. Steam whistles out of your ears, like a kettle.
Twelve glasses of water later, the bowl is empty. Your photo goes up on the wall, under a big gold sign: Dragon Fire Champion!
That's the dragon fire ending!
One spicy miso ramen, extra egg! Order up!
First slurp. Your whole face relaxes for the first time all day.
And in your hand, your change: one single, shiny penny. The staff worked very hard today. Do you want to drop your penny in the tip jar?
One spicy miso ramen, extra egg! Order up!
First slurp. Pure happiness. And this time, you've got two dollars and twenty-three cents in change.
Through the window, you spot the delivery courier, sitting on the curb, still looking very sorry. Do you want to invite him in to share your noodles?
You wave him inside, and push your bowl into the middle of the table.
For me? Even after I bonked your nose with a door?
You spend your change on a plate of dumplings to share, and Chef Slurpy sends over a second bowl of ramen.
Friends eat free at Slurpy's!
Two full tummies. One brand new friend. And the best noodles in the whole city.
That's the friendship ending! The rarest ending of all!
Nope. This bowl is all yours. Every. Last. Noodle.
Then you spend your change on a pink mochi for dessert, and eat it in one squishy bite.
You lean back with a tummy as round as a beach ball. It's been a long day. But it was worth it.
That's the full tummy ending!
You slip the penny into your pocket. Every great fortune starts with one penny, right?
You slurp the rest of your noodles, very pleased with yourself, and very, very full.
That's the hoarder ending!
Clink! Your penny drops into the tip jar.
A tip! For us? Somebody get me a tissue.
The whole kitchen gives you a little bow, and Chef Slurpy slips an extra egg into your bowl.
That's the grateful ending! The best ending of all!
While Chef Slurpy's back is turned, you ladle yourself a secret bowl.
Mid-slurp, a big hand lands on your shoulder.
If you eat in my kitchen, you wash in my kitchen!
Five hundred dirty bowls later, your fingers are as wrinkly as noodles.
That's the busted ending!
You tiptoe through the back door, into the kitchen. Steam everywhere. Pots bubbling. And Chef Slurpy, cooking five orders at once, with his back to you.
Two misos! Three dumplings! Where's my egg?!
A pot of ramen is bubbling right next to you, and nobody is looking. Do you want to sneak yourself a bowl?
No sneaking. Instead, you grab an apron, roll up your sleeves, and start helping. You stir. You chop. You catch a flying egg.
Who are you? Never mind. You're hired!
When the rush is over, Chef Slurpy cooks you a bowl himself, and whispers his secret recipe in your ear.
Extra love. And a pinch of pepper.
That's the apprentice ending!
